Implementation and tests for Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are present and passing.
1) Rule implementation - File: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - Top-level JSDoc explicitly ties the rule to this story and its requirements: - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` - `@req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING`, `REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT`, `REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX`, `REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT`, `REQ-VALID-OUTPUT`, `REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION`, `REQ-AUTO-FIX` - Key behaviors: - Optional warning (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING / Configurable Enforcement REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY): - Rule meta: `{ type: "suggestion", docs: { recommended: false } }` so it is *not* included by default in presets and is controlled only by ESLint severity configuration. - `processComment` inspects block comments; when legacy `@story` + `@req` is found, it calls `context.report({ messageId: "preferImplements", ... })`. - Auto-fix support (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): - `meta.fixable = "code"`. - `collectStoryAndReqMetadata` parses a comment, collecting: - `storyLineIndices` (lines with `@story`), `reqLineIndices` (lines with `@req`), `reqIds` (requirement IDs), `storyPath` (single path if valid). - It only accepts simple forms `@story ` and `@req `; complex forms cause `storyPath` to be set to `null` so no fix is attempted (satisfying REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - `buildImplementsAutoFix`: - Requires `storyPaths.size === 1`, exactly one story line, at least one req line, and non-null `storyPath` (enforces REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX). - Builds a fixer via `applyImplementsReplacement`. - `applyImplementsReplacement`: - Constructs a new `@supports ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}` line. - Derives `linePrefix` from the original `@story` line (`/^(\s*\*?\s*)/`), so indentation and leading `*` are preserved (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT). - Produces `fixedLines` that: - Replace the `@story` line with the `@supports` line - Remove all `@story` and `@req` lines - Leave all other lines untouched (including description, @param, etc.), thereby preserving comment structure and order. - Uses `fixer.replaceTextRange` to update only the block comment’s text, keeping the surrounding `/*` and `*/` delimiters. - Multi-story detection & non-fixable cases (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): - `analyzeComment` populates `storyPaths` and flags presence of `@supports`. - `hasMultipleStories` compares `storyPaths.size` to `MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD = 1`. - `processComment` logic: - If comment mixes `@story`/`@req` and `@supports` → reports `messageId: "cannotAutoFix"` with data.reason = "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @supports annotations". - If more than one story path → reports `messageId: "multiStoryDetected"` and *does not* auto-fix. - Otherwise, calls `buildImplementsAutoFix` and reports `preferImplements` with a fixer if available; when the pattern is too complex (e.g., complex @req or @story lines), `fix` is `null`, so the rule still warns but does not modify code (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - Backward compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): - `processComment` immediately returns if either `hasStory` or `hasReq` is false, meaning comments with only `@story`, only `@req`, or only `@supports` are ignored by this rule and remain governed solely by the existing validation rules. - When the rule is disabled (default in presets), it has no effect (see plugin configs below).
2) Plugin configuration / default severity (Configurable Enforcement: REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY and Both Formats Valid: REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION) - File: src/index.ts - `RULE_NAMES` includes "prefer-implements-annotation", so the rule is part of the plugin’s rule set. - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` *does not* include `"traceability/prefer-implements-annotation"`, so: - Built-in `recommended` and `strict` configs created by `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()` omit this rule entirely. - This ensures the rule is disabled by default in first-party presets. - Tests explicitly validate this behavior: - File: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - In the "configuration severity" describe block: - Asserts that `configs.recommended[0].rules["traceability/prefer-implements-annotation"]` is `undefined`. - Asserts same for `configs.strict[0]`. - Confirms that flat config objects can set the rule to `"warn"` or `"error"`, demonstrating configurable enforcement via ESLint severity (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY).
3) Tests for this story and its requirements - File: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - File header: - `Tests for: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` - `@req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING`, `REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT`, `REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY` - Behavior tests (using RuleTester): - Valid cases (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): 1) `comment with only @story is ignored` 2) `comment with only @req is ignored` 3) `comment with @supports only is ignored` These show that legacy-only and supports-only comments do not trigger this rule, preserving existing validation semantics. - Invalid cases covering the main requirements: - `[REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING] single-story @story + @req block triggers preferImplements message` - Asserts an error with `messageId: "preferImplements"`. - Expects `output` where the `@story`/`@req` block is converted to a single `@supports ...` line — exercising REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, and REQ-VALID-OUTPUT. - `[REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT] mixed @story/@req and @supports triggers cannotAutoFix` - Asserts an error with `messageId: "cannotAutoFix"` and reason `"comment mixes @story/@req with existing @supports annotations"` — multi-story / mixed usage detection without auto-fix (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - `[REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT] multiple @story paths in same block trigger multiStoryDetected` - Asserts an error with `messageId: "multiStoryDetected"` for multiple distinct @story paths (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT). - `[REQ-AUTO-FIX] single @story + single @req auto-fixes to single @supports line` - Similar to the earlier case, but specifically validates the auto-fixed output for a single requirement (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT implicitly via correct replacement within the block). - `[REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX] single @story with multiple @req lines auto-fixes to single @supports line containing all REQ IDs` - Confirms that multiple simple `@req` lines are consolidated into a single `@supports` line with all IDs (REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - `[REQ-AUTO-FIX] complex @req content (extra description) does not auto-fix but still warns` - Asserts `preferImplements` error without an `output`, implying no fix applied for complex patterns (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT: avoid unsafe fixes while still recommending migration). - `[REQ-AUTO-FIX] complex @story content (extra description) does not auto-fix but still warns` - Same idea for complex @story content (also REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - Configuration tests directly target REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY and default-off behavior. - All tests, including this suite, pass: - From `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` (already executed): - `PASS tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts` - The log shows both the main behavior suite and the configuration severity suite executing successfully.
4) Quality and validity of auto-fix output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT) - Auto-fix output format: - `@supports ...` as constructed in `applyImplementsReplacement`. - Compatibility with existing validation rules: - Other tests confirm that `valid-annotation-format` accepts this `@supports` format (e.g., tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts under requirements `REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE`, `REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT` verify valid `@supports` syntax and patterns). - `valid-req-reference` tests (`tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts`) exercise `@supports` with requirement IDs and show that such annotations are valid when story paths and IDs are correct. - Because the auto-fix simply reuses a valid `@story` path and plain `@req` IDs from already-valid comments, and rewrites them into a `@supports` line, the resulting comments inherently satisfy `valid-annotation-format` and `valid-req-reference` expectations, aligning with REQ-VALID-OUTPUT.
5) Documentation: Migration guide with auto-fix examples and opt-in configuration (Documentation acceptance criterion) - File: user-docs/migration-guide.md - User-facing migration guide (in user-docs/ as required) with attribution: `Created autonomously by [voder.ai](https://voder.ai)`. - Includes a dedicated section: "Optional `prefer-implements-annotation` migration rule" that explains: - The rule is disabled by default and not in any presets. - How to enable it in ESLint configuration (`"warn"`/`"error"`). - That it provides conservative auto-fixes from `@story` + `@req` to `@supports`. - Contains concrete examples of annotations and comments about how the rule participates in migration workflows. - File: docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md (developer/internal documentation) - Documents rule behavior, diagnostics (`preferImplements`, `cannotAutoFix`, `multiStoryDetected`), and configuration patterns. - Shows before/after examples with `@story`/`@req` being converted to `@supports`. - Reinforces that the rule is opt-in and that validation behavior remains unchanged, matching the story’s intent.
6) Other acceptance criteria mapping - **Optional Warning**: Implemented and tested (rule emits `preferImplements` warnings for eligible comments; disabled by default; controlled via severity) — REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING. - **Auto-fix Support**: Implemented via `buildImplementsAutoFix` and `applyImplementsReplacement`, with Jest tests asserting `output` for single and multi-req cases — REQ-AUTO-FIX. - **Single Story Conversion**: Strictly enforced in code (one story path, one @story line) and validated via test `"single @story with multiple @req lines auto-fixes to single @supports line"` — REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX. - **Multi-story Detection**: Implemented with `hasMultipleStories` and `messageId: "multiStoryDetected"`, plus `cannotAutoFix` for mixed `@supports` usage; both behaviors covered in tests — REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT. - **Preserve Order / JSDoc structure**: `applyImplementsReplacement` only replaces/removes `@story` and `@req` lines while preserving all other comment lines and original indentation/`*` prefix; tests verify correct transformed comments and unchanged surrounding structure, satisfying REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT in practice. - **Configurable Enforcement**: Verified by `prefer-implements-annotation configuration severity` tests and by absence of the rule from built-in configs — REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY. - **Both Formats Valid**: Valid tests show that comments with only `@story`, only `@req`, or only `@supports` are accepted by this rule, and other validation rules (tested in their own suites) remain unchanged. With the rule disabled by default in presets, legacy annotations continue to behave as before — REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION. - **Quality Standards / Valid Output**: Auto-fix output format aligns with what `valid-annotation-format` and `valid-req-reference` expect for `@supports`, and the rule deliberately skips complex patterns to avoid invalid transformations — REQ-VALID-OUTPUT. - **Documentation**: The user-facing migration guide and internal rule documentation provide auto-fix examples and opt-in configuration, matching the documentation acceptance criterion.
All related Jest tests, including those specifically referencing this story (tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts), pass successfully in the full `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` run.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and requirements for Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented. The `prefer-implements-annotation` rule exists, is disabled by default, provides configurable recommendations, performs conservative auto-fix from @story/@req to @supports for single-story cases, detects and reports non-fixable multi-story/mixed patterns, preserves JSDoc structure, keeps legacy annotations valid when disabled, produces @supports annotations compatible with existing validation rules, and is documented in both internal rule docs and the user-facing migration guide. Tests explicitly tied to this story pass and cover the required behaviors, including configuration severity and auto-fix transformations.
